req.title: Redirect preserves relative or absolute style
req.statement: The system shall emit relative URLs on /redirect/<n> and absolute URLs on /absolute-redirect/<n>.
triggers: redirect preserves relative or absolute style

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that GET /redirect/<n> emits relative URLs (by default) and GET /absolute-redirect/<n> emits absolute URLs. The source code shows redirect_n_times uses request.args.get('absolute','false') to toggle behaviour, and _redirect/url_for with _external flag controls relative vs absolute. Tests must: (1) verify default /redirect/<n> produces a relative Location header, (2) verify /redirect/<n>?absolute=true produces an absolute Location header, (3) test boundary n=1 (the special-cased branch in source), (4) test n=2 (multi-hop path), (5) test invalid n=0 (negative path, triggers assert). We drive the Flask test client with follow_redirects=False to inspect the raw Location header on each hop.

tests.name: test_redirect_n1_default_relative_location
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
n=1 is the boundary where the special-case branch fires (n==1 path in redirect_n_times)
expected: Location header starts with '/' (relative URL, not http:// or https://)
Location header does NOT start with 'http'
trace: Source lines 537-563: n==1 branch calls url_for('view_get', _external=False) when absolute==False
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_n1_default_relative_location():
    r = client.get('/redirect/1', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r.status_code == 302
    location = r.headers['Location']
    assert location.startswith('/'), f"Expected relative URL starting with '/', got: {location}"
    assert not location.startswith('http'), f"Expected relative URL, got absolute: {location}"

test_redirect_n1_default_relative_location()

tests.name: test_redirect_n1_boundary_relative_vs_absolute_toggle
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
n=1 is the exact boundary where the special-case branch fires
Tests both sides of the absolute boolean condition
actions: Assert exact URL style for each
expected: Default and absolute=false both yield relative Location (starts with '/')
trace: R-HTTPBIN-042: both sides of absolute boolean at n=1 boundary
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_n1_boundary_relative_vs_absolute_toggle():
    r_default = client.get('/redirect/1', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r_default.status_code == 302
    loc_default = r_default.headers['Location']
    assert loc_default.startswith('/'), f"Default should be relative, got: {loc_default}"
    assert not loc_default.startswith('http'), f"Default must not be absolute: {loc_default}"

    r_false = client.get('/redirect/1?absolute=false', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r_false.status_code == 302
    loc_false = r_false.headers['Location']
    assert loc_false.startswith('/'), f"absolute=false should be relative, got: {loc_false}"
    assert not loc_false.startswith('http'), f"absolute=false must not be absolute: {loc_false}"

    r_true = client.get('/redirect/1?absolute=true', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r_true.status_code == 302
    loc_true = r_true.headers['Location']
    assert loc_true.startswith('http'), f"absolute=true should be absolute, got: {loc_true}"
    assert '://' in loc_true, f"absolute=true must contain '://', got: {loc_true}"

test_redirect_n1_boundary_relative_vs_absolute_toggle()

from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_n3_full_chain_relative():
    r1 = client.get('/redirect/3', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r1.status_code == 302
    loc1 = r1.headers['Location']
    assert loc1.startswith('/'), f"Hop1 must be relative, got: {loc1}"
    assert not loc1.startswith('http'), f"Hop1 must not be absolute: {loc1}"

    r2 = client.get(loc1, follow_redirects=False)
    assert r2.status_code == 302
    loc2 = r2.headers['Location']
    assert loc2.startswith('/'), f"Hop2 must be relative, got: {loc2}"
    assert not loc2.startswith('http'), f"Hop2 must not be absolute: {loc2}"

    r3 = client.get(loc2, follow_redirects=False)
    assert r3.status_code == 200

test_redirect_n3_full_chain_relative()

tests.name: test_redirect_absolute_case_insensitive_false
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
absolute param value 'TRUE' (uppercase) should NOT be treated as true per .lower() == 'true' logic
expected: Location header starts with 'http' because .lower() normalises 'TRUE' to 'true'
Confirms case-insensitive handling of the absolute param
trace: R-HTTPBIN-042: absolute param is lowercased before comparison
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_absolute_case_insensitive_false():
    r = client.get('/redirect/1?absolute=TRUE', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r.status_code == 302
    location = r.headers['Location']
    # .lower() means 'TRUE' == 'true' => absolute mode
    assert location.startswith('http'), (
        f"absolute=TRUE should be treated as absolute after .lower(), got: {location}"
    )
    assert '://' in location, f"Expected absolute URL with '://', got: {location}"

test_redirect_absolute_case_insensitive_false()
